_note: Generative-design setup for the tripod base, in the preserve / obstacle / design_space form (topo_setup.py + topo_opt.py). The older topo_study.json is the same problem written in the legacy keep_in/keep_out schema; keep both so the two can be compared.

geometry._preserve_why: the pedestal top carries the camera interface and the M5 hinge, and the three pads are what touches the desk. Sized to sit fully inside the design space: the pedestal tapers to 22 x 19 at the top (ped_top_x/y in the .scad), and the disc is only r=52, so a foot of r=8 centred at r=47 would hang 3 mm over the edge.

obstacle._why: the M5 thumb screw is knurled to 22 mm across. Its knob and the nut have to sit outboard of the fingers, on the hinge axis at z=23, and the measured failure of the first version was the hub rim leaving 0.25 mm of material in the way at x = +-19. That is the constraint, written down. r = 11.75, not 11.0: a Ø22 knob does not go into a Ø22 pocket (the printed v1 measured a Ø21.90 clear envelope), so the pocket carries knob_fit = 0.75 in the .scad and the obstacle has to match it.

_regions_why: every load and support region is a subset of a preserve body -- topo_setup.py rejects the study otherwise, because a load on free material lets the optimiser delete the thing being pushed on. mx_front/mx_back centroids sit at y = +-7.0, so the 1950 N*mm hinge moment is a 139.3 N couple over a 14 mm lever.

cases.name: LC1f  push 30 N from the front at the camera top
cases._note: 30 N at 88 mm becomes 30 N shear plus Mx 1950 N*mm on the pedestal top; the moment is applied as a +-139.3 N couple over the 14 mm lever.

cases.name: LC1b  push 30 N from the back at the camera top
LC2   crush 150 N down on the mount
LC3x  prise 150 N on one foot, the other two clamped
cases._note: the case the current design fails at SF 1.95, so it has to be in the optimisation, not just the check.
